A re-entrant caller would silently discard prior run findings. No current execution path does this; single-call-per-process constraint remains undocumented. Unchanged by fr1.

findings.claim: scp_policy_check_run creates conftest_json via mktemp (lib/policy_check_invocation.sh:156) with no cleanup trap for the Python parse failure path. rm -f fires at line 168 on conftest invocation failure and at line 226 on success, but if the inline python3 at line 173 exits non-zero, set -euo pipefail (now active in the lib) causes immediate function return without reaching line 226, leaking the temp file.
findings.evidence: lib/policy_check_invocation.sh:156: conftest_json="$(mktemp ...scp-conftest.XXXXXX.json)". Line 167-171: rm -f on conftest failure path. Line 173: python3 inline heredoc begins. Line 226: rm -f on success path. No trap 'rm -f "$conftest_json"' RETURN or equivalent anywhere. set -euo pipefail at lib line 2 means any non-zero python3 exit jumps past line 226.
findings.impact: A malformed Conftest JSON output (e.g., memory-starved truncated write, encoding error) leaks one .json temp file per run. File contains only policy-findings data — no credentials. /tmp is cleared on reboot; impact is cosmetic on ephemeral CI runners and typical dev machines. No correctness regression in findings output: the error path is already an infra failure.
findings.mitigation: Add `trap 'rm -f "${conftest_json:-}"' RETURN` immediately after line 156 (bash 4.0+ RETURN pseudo-signal fires when the function returns for any reason). Alternatively register the cleanup with the calling script's EXIT trap by exporting the path.

r1_closures.evidence: policy-check.yml:116-137 defines read_lockfile_field() that reads at runtime from Path(os.environ["SCP_RUNTIME_ROOT"]) / "scripts" / "scp-policy-check.lock". CI now executes two-stage Conftest verification: archive digest checked at policy-check.yml:192 against CONFTST_ARCHIVE_SHA256 (lockfile.conftest.{platform}.archive_sha256); extracted binary checked at line 217 against CONFTST_BINARY_SHA256 (lockfile.conftest.{platform}.sha256). Local script mirrors: archive at scp-policy-check:287 against archive_sha256; binary at line 301 against sha256. Both paths now exercise identical two-stage sequence against the same lockfile fields. scp-policy-check:10-15 adds SECURITY WARNING comment block naming all three sensitive overrides. Line 23: ALLOW_ENV_OVERRIDES=0 as default. Lines 55-71: --allow-env-overrides flag parsed from argv. Lines 73-98: check_sensitive_overrides() detects any active sensitive override and exits 1 unless ALLOW_ENV_OVERRIDES==1, emitting 'refusing testing-only override(s)'. Called at line 351 before any download or execution. Python layer strips overrides in policy_check.py:_prepare_env_for_script (lines 54-64) before delegating to shell, adding a second enforcement layer. lib/policy_check_invocation.sh:2 now contains set -euo pipefail as the first non-comment executable line. All function-level failures in scp_policy_check_init_outputs, scp_policy_check_run, and scp_policy_check_threshold_ok now propagate correctly to the caller regardless of the caller's shell options. When sourced by a caller that had set +e, the lib now enables errexit in the caller's context — intentional per the stated mitigation.

scp-policy-check:227-228 (download_opa) and lines 273-274 (download_conftest) both add chmod 0700 on the cache subdirectory after mkdir -p. Line 367-368 adds chmod 0700 on CACHE_ROOT itself. This restricts directory-write access to the owning user, reducing the TOCTOU race window to same-uid scenarios where the attacker already has full user-level access. lib/policy_check_invocation.sh:42-62 adds scp_policy_check_verify_runtime_binary, which re-hashes each binary immediately before the conftest invocation (called at line 149), further narrowing the exploitation window. Binaries are still installed -m 0755 (world-executable); restricting binary permissions to 0700 remains tracked as carry-forward R1-SBP-MIN-04.
